Subject: Order Form indemnity — follow up on third-party claim carveouts

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal reviewed the MSA + Order Form and flagged two items on indemnity that will block signature unless we find a middle ground:

- BrightLoop needs a carveout for third-party IP claims tied to the model training data (they want the vendor to defend/indemnify if infringement arises from model outputs).
- They want a $5M cap to apply per claim rather than per order form aggregate; our standard is aggregate per year.

I've attached their annotated Order Form (BrightLoop_MSARedlines_v2.docx). Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility on (1) scope (training-data vs product-output) and (2) cap structure? We are aiming to close by EOW and would prefer a clean one-page compromise to circulate to execs.

Best,
Jillian Harper
Senior Counsel, BrightLoop Inc.

Jillian — thanks for the note and the doc. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Neha (product) to weigh in on technical risk.

Quick reactions:
- Scope: Redwood is comfortable drawing a line between claims that arise from (A) customer-supplied content or prompt/data vs (B) model outputs generated from our shared public models. We typically resist taking responsibility for claims tied solely to customer prompts, but we can consider a narrowly written "model-output" indemnity tied to our model training provenance.
- Caps: We can discuss per-claim vs aggregate but need to understand BrightLoop's loss profile and whether they require separate escrow/insurance.

Kimberly/Neha — can you review the attached redlines and propose 2 compromise language options: (1) limited model-output indemnity with an evidence & notice workflow, and (2) a fallback where cap remains aggregate but with an increased per-claim floor. If possible, include the operational steps (who collects evidence, timeline for notice, and who leads defense).

Hi all,

Thanks — I reviewed BrightLoop's redlines. To keep this moving toward signature while protecting Redwood's exposure, I propose two concrete options we can present as a one-paragraph compromise (legal + ops):

Option A (narrow model-output indemnity) — acceptable if BrightLoop: (i) defines the claim as arising from Redwood's proprietary training datasets or model code (not customer prompts or customer-uploaded data); (ii) agrees to Redwood's notice and mitigation process; and (iii) limits Redwood's defense obligation to claims where Redwood has control of remediation. Cap: $3M per claim, aggregate $6M per 12-month period.

Operational notes for Option A:
- Evidence owner: BrightLoop to provide initial claim packet (notice, alleged infringing output, prompt/context, timestamps).
- Redwood will have 30 days to accept or tender defense; if accepted, Redwood leads defense with right to select counsel.
- If BrightLoop withholds critical evidence, Redwood's obligations will be limited.

Option B (cap compromise) — if BrightLoop insists on per-claim $5M, Redwood requests a carveout reducing scope to only third-party claims that are traceable to Redwood-managed model training artifacts AND a requirement that BrightLoop first pursue any available insurance or third-party recovery (subrogation). Cap: $5M per claim, aggregate cap remains $10M per 12-month period.

Additional asks from Redwood:
- Administrative SLA for evidence (72-hour initial acknowledgement, 14-day evidence bundle window).
- Right to escalate to an executive dispute panel (GTM + Legal) for any ambiguous claim determination with a 7-business-day rapid review.

I attached a redline snippet (see BrightLoop_MSARedlines_v2.docx expectations) and a short evidence checklist (evidence-request-checklist.pdf) to standardize submissions.

If BrightLoop is comfortable with Option A or B, Mateo please propose which one you'd like to table to them today. I recommend Option A for lower residual risk.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — third-party claim scope & caps (proposed path forward)

Hi Jillian / BrightLoop team — appreciate the quick turnaround. After discussion with Legal and Product, Redwood's recommended path to keep momentum: present BrightLoop with Option A (narrow model-output indemnity) as our preferred solution, and Option B as a fallback if your execs insist on a $5M per-claim number.

Summary proposal to circulate to your execs (copy/paste-friendly):
- Redwood will indemnify and defend third-party IP claims where the claim is demonstrably caused by Redwood's proprietary training data or model code (explicitly excluding claims solely caused by customer prompts or customer-uploaded data).
- Cap: $3M per claim, $6M aggregate per 12-month period.
- Evidence & notice: BrightLoop to provide claim packet; Redwood to acknowledge within 72 hours and accept/tender defense within 30 days. If BrightLoop cannot provide necessary evidence, Redwood's obligations are limited.
- Executive rapid review: 7-business-day panel to resolve disputes about causation.

If BrightLoop needs the $5M per-claim figure, we can offer Option B with $5M per claim but $10M aggregate and the same evidence/notice requirements plus insurance-first subrogation.

Next steps:
1) Jillian — confirm which option BrightLoop prefers by EOB tomorrow.
2) If Option B is chosen, share any insurance details and we will run a quick risk estimate with our finance team.
3) If Option A is chosen, I will circulate a one-paragraph redline and request countersignature routing.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
